Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Branch: feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches. This is a REWORK round (round 2) on SFCC-91 Step 3, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/`. Do not stage, do not commit. Do not touch any other file in this repo — not `product-view/index.tsx`, not the Step 2 atom, nothing outside this one folder.

A prior round built this molecule correctly in almost every respect, but the Scorer found a real, empirically-reproduced defect plus two smaller issues. Fix exactly these three things, nothing else — everything else about this component (the recipe, the AC 5/AC 1 filter logic, the pagination click mechanics, the keyboard handling, the atom composition) was independently verified correct twice and must not be touched.

## Fix 1 (blocker) — initial page must contain the actual selection, and must stay correct if selection changes

Read `index.tsx` in full first. Currently: `const [pageStart, setPageStart] = useState(0);` — this always shows page 1 (items 0-3) on mount, regardless of where `selectedValue` sits in the `populated` array. Confirmed via a real render test: with 6 populated colours and `selectedValue` set to the 6th one, the component renders items 0-3 with **zero** items `aria-checked`, and **zero** items with `tabindex="0"` — the entire visible radiogroup becomes untabbable, and the real selection is invisible, because the roving-tabindex formula (`isSelected || (!selectedValue && index === 0)`) only ever evaluates against whatever page happens to be showing.

The fix must do BOTH of these, not just one:
1. Compute the page that actually contains the selection: `const selectedIndex = populated.findIndex((value) => value.value === selectedValue);` then the page start is `selectedIndex === -1 ? 0 : Math.floor(selectedIndex / SWATCHES_PER_PAGE) * SWATCHES_PER_PAGE`.
2. This must be correct BOTH at initial mount AND if `selectedValue` (or `populated`) changes while the component instance stays mounted (no remount) — a `useState(() => ...)` lazy initializer only handles the mount case, and per Scorer's explicit finding, this component's structure makes staleness directly observable (unlike base SFCC's version, where `isFocusable` is derived fresh from props every render regardless of a similar mount-only effect it has — that base precedent is NOT safe to copy here, because here `pageStart` gates which items are even rendered, not just which one shows a highlight).

The cleanest correct shape: don't let local state be the sole source of truth for which page is showing when nothing has been manually paged yet. One good approach — track local pagination as an *offset from the selection's natural page*, or use a `useEffect` keyed on `selectedValue`/`populated` that resyncs `pageStart` to the selection's page whenever those change, while still letting manual prev/next clicks move `pageStart` independently in between. Use your own judgement on the exact implementation shape, but the acceptance bar is: (a) mount with a distant selection shows the correct page with the correct item checked and tabbable, AND (b) if you simulate `selectedValue` changing via a prop update on an already-mounted instance (e.g. in a test using `rerender`), the page updates to follow the new selection rather than staying stuck on wherever a user had manually paged to. Manual prev/next clicks must still work exactly as before (that mechanic already tested clean and must not regress).

**Required new test in `index.test.tsx`**: render with more than 4 populated colours and `selectedValue` pointing at one beyond the first page (e.g. the same 6-colour/6th-selected shape used above). On the very first render (no interaction, no `fireEvent`/`userEvent` call), assert exactly one element has `aria-checked="true"` and exactly one element has `tabindex="0"` (as a DOM attribute, via `toHaveAttribute`), and that both point at the actual selected colour, not just any element. This is required — Scorer's instruction is explicit that this exact scenario must be provably covered going forward, since nothing currently shipped could ever catch a regression of this bug.

## Fix 2 (should-fix) — remove the fabricated citation

`index.tsx` around line 156 has a comment reading approximately: *"...is expressed as direct Chakra props with var(--zimm-*) values instead, per overrideStyling.md's 'your call' allowance for this one sub-piece."* This citation is false — the phrase "your call" does not appear anywhere in `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` or any other rules file in this repo (independently confirmed by grep, twice, by two different reviewers). Rewrite the comment to state the actual reasoning without citing a rule that doesn't exist — something like: this is a structural choice for this one static, non-interactive wrapper; it doesn't get a dedicated recipe part because the "one canonical styling surface per component type" rule is scoped to components with competing/interactive style definitions, which doesn't clearly apply to a one-off static layout wrapper like this. Do not invent a different fake citation — either state the reasoning plainly with no citation, or cite something real if you can find an applicable rule; if genuinely unsure, plain reasoning with no citation is the safe choice.

## Fix 3 (should-fix) — add truncation regression coverage

Figma's own interaction annotation on the source node ("If Label/Colour name is longer, use truncation") is correctly implemented today (confirmed: the dynamic colour-name span resolves `overflow:hidden; textOverflow:ellipsis; whiteSpace:nowrap`, the static "Colour:" text does not) but has zero test coverage. Add one test to `index.test.tsx`: render with a long `selectedName` (60+ characters), and assert via `getComputedStyle` on the dynamic name element that `overflow` is `'hidden'`, `textOverflow` is `'ellipsis'`, and `whiteSpace` is `'nowrap'`. Optionally also assert the static "Colour:" label element does NOT have these (e.g. its `textOverflow` should not be `'ellipsis'`) to prove the truncation is scoped to the right element, not both.

## What NOT to do

Do not touch the AC 5 filter, the AC 1 count-gate, the pagination click handlers' existing logic (only the initial/resync page-selection logic per Fix 1), the keyboard arrow handling, the recipe file, the story file (a new story is not required this round — only the required test above), or anything about how `ZimmColourSwatch`/`ZimmIcon` are imported or used. All of that was independently verified correct twice already and re-litigating it is scope creep this round doesn't need.

## Verification — run yourself, report exact output

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run lint
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.test.tsx
npm run test
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
grep -n "your call" overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx
```

Expected: `tsc` 0 errors. The scoped test run should show all original 8 tests still passing PLUS your 2 new tests (10 total), including the new on-mount pagination test actually passing (not just present) and the new truncation test passing. `npm run test` should show 28 files (same as before this rework — you're adding tests to an existing file, not a new file) with 428 tests (426 + 2 new). `lint`/`audit:tokens` unchanged from baseline. The final grep must return nothing (confirms the fabricated citation is gone).

**Also, do a real check on the resync behaviour, not just the mount case**: write a quick throwaway test (can be deleted after, or keep it if it's cheap and adds real value — your call) using `rerender` from Testing Library to change `selectedValue` from one that's on page 1 to one that's on page 2 (or vice versa) on an already-mounted instance, and confirm the visible page actually updates to follow it. Report this result explicitly, even if you don't keep the test — Scorer specifically flagged that a mount-only fix would NOT be sufficient and wants this behaviour proven, not just the initial-render case.

Report back: full command output, confirmation only `index.tsx` and `index.test.tsx` were changed (check `git status`/`git diff --stat` yourself), and the explicit resync-behaviour proof.
